questions.prompt: A joint is excited only with q = 0.01 sin(2t). Torque is fit as I*qdd + b*qd + c*sin(q). Which statement is right?
options: I is identified exactly but c is not.
All three parameters are identified, since the fit error is tiny.
Only b and the combination c - 4I are identified; I and c individually are not.
b is not identified because qd is small.
questions.explanation: qdd = -4q and sin q ~ q are proportional: only c - w^2 I is determined.

questions.prompt: Free decay: successive peaks 1.0 and 0.8, damped period 1.5 s. Compute b/I = 2*ln(p1/p2)/Td in 1/s. Precision 0.001.
With theta=(I,b,c)=(1.5,0.2,8) predict the torque for qdd=2, qd=-1, sin q=0.5. Precision 0.01.
questions.skillLabel: Write a model linear in its parameters

questions.prompt: Acceleration from a second difference of position with sigma_q=0.002 rad and dt=0.02 s: noise sigma_a = sqrt(6)*sigma_q/dt^2 in rad/s^2. Precision 0.01.
A fit has RMSE 0.002 N m on its training data. What do you need before trusting it?
options: Prediction error on a different trajectory, compared with the noise level.
A still lower RMSE measured on the same training data, below the noise.
A larger sampling rate so the same data can be fitted more finely.
A higher-order model so the training RMSE can be driven down further.

questions.prompt: Which is the best way to get acceleration for the regression from noisy 100 Hz position data?
options: Multiply the measured torque by dt to obtain the acceleration directly.
Take the second difference of the raw position samples at the sample rate.
Use an IMU, or smooth first, or use an integral (weak) form of the equation.
Fit with fewer samples so that there is less noise to amplify in the result.

questions.prompt: Design an experiment to identify inertia, damping and gravity coefficient of a one-link joint: excitation, duration, what you record, and how you validate.
rubric: Chooses a multi-frequency or chirp excitation with amplitude and duration and explains why one frequency fails.
Records torque, position and velocity/acceleration with sample rate and addresses noise in differentiation.
Fits with least squares, reports condition number or standard errors, and validates on a different trajectory with a stated tolerance.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
